title: A Per-Pixel Baseline Overstates the AlphaEarth Embedding's Advantage: A Context-Matched Test on Small-Parcel Coffee Boundary Delineation (research package)
description: Research package (reproducible pipeline, confirmatory protocol and figure code) for a study of small-parcel coffee boundary delineation in Minas Gerais, Brazil (2017), using CONAB/fiboa br_conab reference parcels. Identical Random Forest and linear probes predict boundary probability from seasonal Sentinel-2, seasonal Sentinel-1 plus Sentinel-2, the AlphaEarth annual embedding and their fusion, per pixel and with the same four neighborhood features (local mean, local standard deviations, gradient) for every input; watershed and region-merging decoders extract parcel objects. The neighborhood-feature control was fixed in a written protocol and tested on 48 new tiles from 36 unused regions: per pixel the embedding ranks boundary pixels better (Boundary AP 0.579 vs 0.449), but with identical neighborhood features seasonal Sentinel-2 exceeds the embedding at exact one-pixel boundary localization (0.664 vs 0.610; Hodges-Lehmann difference -0.052, 95% CI -0.063 to -0.043); with a one-pixel tolerance the two tie. In this setting, the per-pixel baseline overstated the embedding's advantage. Includes reference extraction, tile sampling, Earth Engine download, probing, decoding, paired statistics (non-superiority, TOST), the protocol with the ordered confirmatory tile list and frozen thresholds, per-tile results, and figure generation. Intermediate data are regenerable from the code with fixed seeds.
